title: Relative flatness and a flat fibre stalk give a free neighbourhood
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, and $\mathcal F_s$ be its tensor pullback to the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] and $(\mathcal F_s)_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then there are an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X$ of $x$ and an integer $r\geq0$ with $\mathcal F|_W\cong\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}$.

proof.text: Suppose first that $\mathcal F_x\otimes\kappa(x)=0$. The stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is finitely generated over the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ because $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation. Apply the Nakayama generating criterion [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the empty family: its image generates the zero residue-fibre, so $\mathcal F_x=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk] to the zero morphism $0\to\mathcal F$. Its stalk map is surjective because $\mathcal F_x=0$, and finite presentation gives finite type. After shrinking to an open neighbourhood $W$ of $x$, $\mathcal F|_W=0$, which is the required conclusion with $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 080Q, proof, first sentence (the zero-fibre case), using Algebra Tag 00DV and Modules Tag 01B8.

e0$. For the fibre, let $p:X_s	o X$ be the first projection and $x'\in X_s$ the point over $x$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $p^\sharp_{x'}$ induces a ring isomorphism $S_x/\mathfrak m_RS_x\cong\mathcal O_{X_s,x'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] applied to $p$ and $\mathcal F$, $(\mathcal F_s)_{x'}=(p^*\mathcal F)_{x'}\cong M\otimes_{S_x}\mathcal O_{X_s,x'}$ as $\mathcal O_{X_s,x'}$-modules, and under the ring isomorphism this is $M\otimes_{S_x}S_x/\mathfrak m_RS_x=M/\mathfrak m_RM$ as an $S_x/\mathfrak m_RS_x$-module. Flatness is invariant under such a compatible pair of isomorphisms, so the hypothesis that $(\mathcal F_s)_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ says that $M/\mathfrak m_RM$ is flat over $S_x/\mathfrak m_RS_x$; the other hypothesis says that $M$ is flat over $R$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre], applied to $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}S_x\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}S_x$ and $M$ (its $S$ and $S'$ both $S_x$), gives that $\mathcal F_x=M$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$.

proof.text: The stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is finitely generated over the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and it is flat by the preceding step. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] gives a finite basis of $\mathcal F_x$ over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$; write its cardinality as $r\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 080Q, proof, sentence “Hence $\mathcal F_x$ is free”, invoking Algebra Tag 00NZ.

proof.text: Represent the $r$ basis vectors by sections on a common open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ and let $\psi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F|_U$ send the standard basis to those sections. Its stalk map at $x$ is surjective (indeed an isomorphism). The restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite type because it is of finite presentation. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk] to $\psi$ and shrinking gives an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $x$ on which $\psi$ is surjective as a sheaf map.

source.place: Tag 080Q, proof, sentences “Choose an open neighbourhood ... sections ... basis” and “The corresponding map ... is surjective after shrinking”, using Modules Tag 01B8.

proof.text: On the ringed space $V$, the module $\mathcal F|_V$ remains finitely presented and $\psi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F|_V$ is surjective. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-kernel-surjection-finite-type] shows that $K=\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)$ is of finite type. At $x$, the map $\psi_x$ is the chosen basis isomorphism, so $K_x=0$.

source.place: Tag 080Q, proof, sentences “Then Ker(ψ) is of finite type” and “Ker(ψ)_x=0”, invoking Modules Tag 01BP.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk] to the zero morphism $0\to K$ at $x$. Since $K$ is of finite type and $K_x=0$, its stalk map is surjective, so after shrinking to an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq V$ we have $K|_W=0$.

source.place: Tag 080Q, proof, sentence “Whence after shrinking U once more ψ is an isomorphism”, with Modules Tag 01B8.

proof.text: The restriction $\psi|_W$ is surjective by construction and has zero kernel, hence is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_W$-modules. Therefore $\mathcal F|_W\cong\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}$, proving the statement.
